items.title: Bounded changes of measure: the finite-integral entropy and energy core

source.anchor: §2.3.1, Proposition2.3.1 proof and entropy-cost display, printed pp60–61
source.attribution: Classical Holley–Stroock mechanism; source exposition by Sinho Chewi. These generic library interfaces are not a claim that the complete geometric proposition has been formalized.

items.statement: For a fixed class of finite-integral tests and a fixed nonnegative energy density, bounded comparison of probability laws transfers entropy and its energy inequality. A bounded exponential tilt has exact transfer factor exp(u-l); normalization and target-law integrability are proved. Geometric base inequalities and extension to larger functional domains remain separate.
assumptions: Both laws in the comparison theorem are probability measures.
All real entropy tests and energy tests use precisely the finite-integral domain of the displayed definition.
The energy density and test predicate remain fixed as the measure changes.

formulae.label: exponential factor
formulae.tex: \nu=Z^{-1}e^B\mu,\quad l\le B\le u\quad\Longrightarrow\quad C_\nu\le C_\mu e^{u-l}.

obligations.label: Canonical finite-integral entropy comparison and fixed-energy transfer underlying the LSI branch

bindings.boundary: Canonical finite-integral interface only. Full geometric test-class and Sobolev extension remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: The background proposition is stated using geometric LSI and oscillation.
assumption_deltas.lean: A fixed arbitrary test predicate and energy density on a measurable probability space, with the finite-integral domain expanded explicitly.
assumption_deltas.reason: This canonical core proves a measure comparison mechanism and does not claim the entire geometric or extended-domain theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: A bounded exponential tilt of a probability law.
assumption_deltas.lean: Almost-everywhere measurable B and finite almost-everywhere bounds l ≤ B ≤ u; exponential integrability is derived in the tilted theorem.
assumption_deltas.reason: These conditions make the density and normalization meaningful; the theorem proves rather than assumes the normalization and density comparisons.
